Three artists · Three weeks Twee Jonge Gezellen, Tulbagh 5–25 July 2027 A programme hosted by Krone, in partnership with ArtThrob and developed with Sue Williamson.
THE PROJECT
ArtThrob and Krone invite applications for a three-week Group Artist Residency at Twee Jonge Gezellen, Tulbagh, in July 2027.
Three artists from different disciplines will be selected to live and work alongside one another for a focused period of research, experimentation and exchange on the farm.

The residency brings different practices into dialogue with one another and with the landscape, history and context of Twee Jonge Gezellen and the surrounding Tulbagh valley. It is intended to create space for artists to develop their individual practices while allowing conversation, proximity and exchange between disciplines to inform the process.

South Africa’s oldest running online magazine, concerned with capturing the written narrative of contemporary South African art since 1997. We are collaborating to explore new ways in which interdisciplinary practise can come together and form new conversations.
Applications are welcomed from artists working across painting, sculpture, installation, photography, film, writing, sound, music and interdisciplinary practices.

One of the three participants is encouraged to have a strong interest in writing or publishing and to take an active role in developing a publication alongside the residency — participating in the group on equal footing and contributing to its thinking as it develops.
During the three weeks, visiting artists, curators, writers and speakers will join the residents for talks, conversations and critical exchange.
The residency may culminate in a group exhibition or another shared outcome developed through the process.
ARTTHROB + KRONE
Founded in 1997, ArtThrob is South Africa’s longest-running online publication dedicated to contemporary art, capturing and contributing to the written narrative of contemporary South African art.
ArtThrob and Krone are collaborating on the residency to explore new ways in which interdisciplinary practices can come together, enter into dialogue and generate new conversations.
TWEE JONGE GEZELLEN

Twee Jonge Gezellen has stood at the foot of the Saronsberg outside Tulbagh since 1710. A working farm for more than three centuries, it is a place shaped by agriculture, landscape, architecture and the histories of the surrounding valley.
The farm provides the context for the residency rather than prescribing its subject. Artists are invited to engage with the place in ways relevant to their own practice and research.

The residency offers accommodation neighbouring the farm, basic studio and workshop facilities, access to the gallery space, and fresh seasonal produce from the farm provided weekly at the shared residency house.
A programme of visiting artists, curators, writers and speakers will punctuate the three weeks, creating opportunities for conversation, critique and exchange.
WHO MAY APPLY
The open call welcomes artists working across painting, sculpture, installation, photography, film, writing, sound, music and interdisciplinary practices.
We are particularly interested in artists who are open to dialogue and exchange, and whose work may benefit from engaging with practitioners working in different disciplines.
Artists may apply individually or as a proposed group of three.
Individual applicants will be brought together by the selection panel, with consideration given to how different practices and perspectives might enter into dialogue with one another.

The call is open to everyone. Local transport and airfares within South Africa, including transfers to and from the farm, are covered by the residency. International applicants are responsible for their own travel to South Africa.
WHAT THE RESIDENCY PROVIDES
Accommodation neighbouring the farm for the full three weeks
Basic studio facilities, workshop and access to the gallery space
Fresh seasonal produce from the farm, provided weekly at the shared residency house
A food allowance
A programme of visiting artists, curators, writers and speakers
Local transport and airfares within South Africa, including transfers to and from the farm
SELECTION PANEL
Applications will be reviewed and discussed by a selection panel bringing together artists, curators, writers and cultural practitioners.
Sue Williamson
Artist
Khanya Mashabala

Nkgopoleng Moloi

The panel will consider the strength of each individual application as well as the potential dialogue between different practices when forming the final group of three residents.

RESIDENCY:
APPLICATIONS Applications may be submitted individually or as a proposed group of three.
Full application requirements and submission guidelines are outlined below. Applying as an individual Please submit a single PDF containing:
Short bio — maximum 150 words
CV — maximum two pages

Statement — maximum 500 words outlining how you envision using your time at the farm. This does not need to be a finished project plan; we would rather understand the question you are carrying, and why this place and context might be useful to it.
Recent work — four to five images, including titles, dates, medium and dimensions. Writers may instead submit two pieces of writing, published or unpublished, up to 2,000 words in total.
Contact details — name, email address, phone number and where you are based.
Optional — Is there something you have been wanting to make, and haven’t been able to? Maximum 100 words.
APPLYING AS A GROUP OF THREE Please submit a single PDF containing:
Please include the individual requirements above for each applicant, plus:
Shared statement — maximum 500 words outlining what you would like to work on together and whY these three practices.
Named contact person for the group.

File name: Surname_Firstname_KroneResidency.pdf
